officialTitle: High-Dose Once-Daily Thoracic Radiotherapy in Limited-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer: CALGB 30610 (Alliance)/RTOG 0538

design.notes: Two-stage design: initially three arms (45 Gy twice daily, 70 Gy once daily, 61.2 Gy concomitant boost); the concomitant-boost arm was discontinued after a planned interim toxicity analysis. Radiotherapy started with the first or second of four chemotherapy cycles.

clinicalQuestion: Does escalating thoracic radiotherapy to a high-dose once-daily regimen improve overall survival compared with twice-daily radiotherapy in limited-stage SCLC?

pico.population: Limited-stage SCLC receiving four cycles of chemotherapy
pico.outcomes: Primary: overall survival (ITT). Severe adverse events

arms.label: 45 Gy twice daily
arms.regimen: Chemotherapy with concurrent twice-daily thoracic radiotherapy
arms.doseSourceQuote: All patients randomly assigned to 45-Gy twice-daily (n = 313) or 70-Gy once-daily radiotherapy (n = 325) are included in this analysis.

arms.label: 70 Gy once daily
arms.regimen: Chemotherapy with concurrent high-dose once-daily thoracic radiotherapy
arms.doseSourceQuote: All patients randomly assigned to 45-Gy twice-daily (n = 313) or 70-Gy once-daily radiotherapy (n = 325) are included in this analysis.

arms.label: 61.2 Gy concomitant boost (discontinued)
arms.regimen: Chemotherapy with concomitant-boost thoracic radiotherapy; arm closed after interim toxicity analysis
arms.doseSourceQuote: In the first stage, patients with limited-stage disease were randomly assigned to receive 45-Gy twice-daily, 70-Gy once-daily, or 61.2-Gy concomitant-boost radiotherapy, starting with either the first or second (of four total) chemotherapy cycles.

publications.title: High-Dose Once-Daily Thoracic Radiotherapy in Limited-Stage Small-Cell Lung Cancer: CALGB 30610 (Alliance)/RTOG 0538.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.population: ITT (45 Gy twice-daily vs 70 Gy once-daily arms)
outcomes.sourceQuote: After a median follow-up of 4.7 years, OS was not improved on the once-daily arm (hazard ratio for death, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.17;= .594). Median survival is 28.5 months for twice-daily treatment, and 30.1 months for once-daily treatment, with 5-year OS of 29% and 32%, respectively.

safety.description: Severe adverse events including oesophageal and pulmonary toxicity were reported as similar between arms (no numbers in abstract)
safety.sourceQuote: Treatment was tolerable, and the frequency of severe adverse events, including esophageal and pulmonary toxicity, was similar on both arms.

strengths: Large NCI-sponsored randomised phase III trial with modern radiotherapy planning
limitations: Superiority design; no improvement shown for the high-dose once-daily arm
Open-label radiotherapy comparison; long accrual period

clinicalImplications.text: High-dose once-daily radiotherapy did not improve overall survival over twice-daily radiotherapy; the authors state twice-daily treatment remains standard while the data inform choice of regimen.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Together with CONVERT, this trial supports twice-daily radiotherapy as the reference schedule, with high-dose once-daily treatment as a tolerable alternative when twice-daily delivery is impractical.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 36623230. A 2026 mature report of the discontinued 61.2 Gy concomitant-boost arm (PMID 42086125) exists but was not ingested.
